claims.text: A hybrid TOR-TILD and machine-learning interpolation approach can improve determination of thermodynamic properties at the solid-to-fluid transition in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
Machine-learning interpolation can make exploration of the compositional space more computationally efficient.
The hybrid approach can reduce computational cost relative to existing computational methods.
The hybrid approach can retain ab initio-level accuracy while using machine-learning interpolation.
The solid-to-fluid transition can be identified from the crossing point of the solid and fluid Gibbs energies.
The hybrid approach will improve the accuracy of transition-temperature determination relative to current experiments and DFT free-energy studies.
The hybrid approach will improve determination of fusion enthalpy and entropy relative to current experiments and DFT free-energy studies.
The hybrid approach will improve determination of the volume change at the transition relative to current experiments and DFT free-energy studies.
The hybrid approach will improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity relative to current experiments and DFT free-energy studies.
The hybrid approach will be more computationally efficient than existing computational methods.
The approach is applicable across relevant high-entropy-material compositions and temperatures.
Machine-learning models may have insufficient accuracy for complex thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning models may fail to represent all thermodynamic effects important to the transition.
